question_english: Which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) serves as the foundational cornerstone for personal liberty by guaranteeing that "Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person"?
options_english: Article 1
Article 3
Article 5
Article 9
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) Article 3.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text and Scope of Article 3: Article 3 of the UDHR succinctly proclaims: 'Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person.' It constitutes the bedrock of civil liberties, forming the gateway right without which no other economic, social, or political right can be exercised.
2. Inherent Triad of Rights:
   - Right to Life: Absolute protection against arbitrary deprivation of life.
   - Right to Liberty: Freedom from unlawful custody, physical restraint, and arbitrary imprisonment.
   - Security of Person: Protection against physical assault, bodily injury, and harassment by state or private actors.
3. Comparison with Indian Constitution: Article 3 of the UDHR directly corresponds to Article 21 of the Constitution of India ('Protection of life and personal liberty: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law'). The Supreme Court of India in landmark decisions (e.g., Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978, and K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017) has interpreted Article 21 in light of Article 3 of the UDHR.
4. Other Articles in Options:
   - Article 1: Equality in dignity and rights, reason and conscience.
   - Article 5: Prohibition of torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment.
   - Article 9: Prohibition of arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) अनुच्छेद 3।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. अनुच्छेद 3 का मूल पाठ एवं क्षेत्र: UDHR का अनुच्छेद 3 घोषणा करता है कि 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को जीवन, स्वतंत्रता और वैयक्तिक सुरक्षा का अधिकार है' (Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person)। यह सभी नागरिक स्वतंत्रताओं का मूल आधार है।
2. तीन मूलभूत घटक:
   (i) जीवन का अधिकार: मनमाने ढंग से जीवन से वंचित किए जाने से सुरक्षा।
   (ii) स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार: गैर-कानूनी बंदी बनाए जाने और शारीरिक प्रतिबंधों से मुक्ति।
   (iii) वैयक्तिक सुरक्षा: राज्य अथवा गैर-राज्य तत्वों द्वारा शारीरिक हिंसा और प्रताड़ना से संरक्षण।

question_english: Article 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) explicitly and unconditionally prohibits which of the following acts?
options_english: Arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile of individuals
Arbitrary interference with personal privacy, family, or correspondence
Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment
Subjection to slavery, servitude, or the transatlantic slave trade
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text of Article 5: Article 5 of the UDHR states in absolute terms: 'No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.'
2. Non-Derogable and Absolute Character: The prohibition against torture is an absolute, non-derogable human right (jus cogens). It cannot be suspended under any circumstances—even during states of war, public emergency, or anti-terror operations. This principle is codified in the UN Convention Against Torture (UNCAT, 1984) and Article 7 of the ICCPR.
3. Indian Jurisprudence: Although India has not yet enacted a specific standalone anti-torture statute, the Supreme Court of India in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997) held that custodial torture, rape, or death violates Article 21 of the Constitution and constitutes a direct assault on human dignity under Article 5 of the UDHR.
4. Mapping of Other Articles:
   - Article 4 prohibits slavery and servitude.
   - Article 9 prohibits arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile.
   - Article 12 prohibits arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) यातना अथवा क्रूर, अमानवीय या अपमानजनक व्यवहार या दंड।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR के अनुच्छेद 5 का मूल पाठ: 'किसी भी व्यक्ति को यातना अथवा क्रूर, अमानवीय या अपमानजनक व्यवहार या दंड के अधीन नहीं किया जाएगा' (No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment)।
2. अनुलंघनीय अधिकार (Non-Derogable Right): यातना का प्रतिषेध अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विधि में एक पूर्ण एवं अहस्तांतरणीय सिद्धांत (Jus Cogens) है। युद्ध, आपातकाल या राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा जैसी किसी भी परिस्थिति में इसका उल्लंघन नहीं किया जा सकता। संयुक्त राष्ट्र का यातना-विरोधी अभिसमय (UNCAT, 1984) इसी सिद्धांत को संहिताबद्ध करता है।
3. भारतीय न्यायशास्त्र: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने डी.के. बसु बनाम पश्चिम बंगाल राज्य (1997) मामले में ऐतिहासिक निर्णय देते हुए गिरफ्तारी और हिरासत के संबंध में सख्त दिशानिर्देश तय किए तथा स्पष्ट किया कि पुलिस हिरासत में यातना संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 और UDHR के अनुच्छेद 5 का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
4. अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 4 दासता पर रोक लगाता है; अनुच्छेद 9 मनमानी गिरफ्तारी व निर्वासन का प्रतिषेध करता है; और अनुच्छेद 12 निजता के अधिकार की रक्षा करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights establishes an absolute, non-derogable prohibition against cruel treatment. It explicitly mandates that no individual shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment under any circumstances, ensuring complete protection of bodily integrity and human dignity across all jurisdictions globally.

question_hindi:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं, एक को अभिकथन (A) और दूसरे को कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है:

अभिकथन (A): मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) की रूपरेखा के अंतर्गत, माता-पिता को यह चुनने का पूर्व अधिकार (Prior Right) प्राप्त है कि उनके बच्चों को किस प्रकार की शिक्षा दी जाएगी।
कारण (R): UDHR के प्रारूपकारों ने यह सुनिश्चित करके कि शैक्षणिक चयन माता-पिता के दार्शनिक और नैतिक विश्वासों का सम्मान करता है, परिवारों को सर्वाधिकारवादी राज्य द्वारा वैचारिक थोपने (Indoctrination) से बचाना चाहा था।

(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):

Assertion (A): Under the framework of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), parents possess a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be provided to their children.
Reason (R): The drafters of the UDHR sought to safeguard families against totalitarian state indoctrination by ensuring that educational choices respect parental philosophical and moral convictions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct option:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true, but (R) is false.
(A) is false, but (R) is true.
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Validity of Assertion (A): Article 26(3) of the UDHR explicitly states: 'Parents have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.' Therefore, Assertion (A) is legally and textually correct.
2. Validity of Reason (R): The historical and legislative intent (travaux préparatoires) behind Article 26(3) reflects the horrific experiences of World War II. Totalitarian regimes (notably Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany via the Hitler Youth / Hitlerjugend) seized absolute monopoly over schools to politically and racially indoctrinate young minds, alienating children from family values and traditional religious/moral principles. The drafters inserted Article 26(3) specifically to counterbalance state power and prevent totalitarian indoctrination.
3. Nexus between (A) and (R): Because the historical motivation directly explains why the prior right of parents was specifically enshrined in Article 26(3), Reason (R) is the accurate and direct explanation of Assertion (A).
4. Indian Jurisprudence: The right of parents to choose appropriate schooling and minority educational autonomy is recognized under Articles 29 and 30 of the Indian Constitution, as well as the Supreme Court's ruling in the TMA Pai Foundation (2002) case.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (a) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. अभिकथन (A) की सत्यता: UDHR के अनुच्छेद 26(3) में स्पष्ट रूप से यह प्रावधान किया गया है कि 'माता-पिता को यह चुनने का पूर्व-अधिकार (Prior Right) है कि उनके बच्चों को किस प्रकार की शिक्षा दी जाएगी।' अतः अभिकथन (A) पूर्णतः सत्य है।
2. कारण (R) की सत्यता: द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान नाजी और फासीवादी शासन ने सरकारी स्कूलों और अनिवार्य युवा संगठनों (जैसे हिटलर यूथ) के माध्यम से बच्चों का नस्लवादी एवं अधिनायकवादी वैचारिक ब्रेनवॉश (Indoctrination) किया था। इस कड़वे अनुभव से सीख लेते हुए UDHR के निर्माताओं ने यह सुनिश्चित किया कि शिक्षा पर राज्य का पूर्ण एकाधिकार न हो तथा माता-पिता अपने धार्मिक, दार्शनिक और सांस्कृतिक मूल्यों के अनुसार बच्चों की शिक्षा तय कर सकें। अतः कारण (R) भी सत्य है।
3. व्याख्या का संबंध: कारण (R) सीधे तौर पर यह स्पष्ट करता है कि अनुच्छेद 26(3) में माता-पिता को यह पूर्वाधिकार क्यों दिया गया था। अतः (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
4. भारतीय संदर्भ: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 30 अल्पसंख्यकों को अपनी पसंद के शिक्षण संस्थान स्थापित करने और प्रशासित करने का अधिकार देता है, जो अभिभावकों की शैक्षणिक पसंद की स्वतंत्रता की पुष्टि करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 26(3) of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights asserts that parents hold a prior right to choose their children’s education. This principle was explicitly designed to safeguard families from forced state indoctrination, ensuring educational decisions align with parents’ moral, philosophical, and religious values while protecting children’s fundamental right to holistic development.

question_hindi: मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) के उत्तरार्ध (अनुच्छेद 22 से 27) में सन्निहित आर्थिक, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक अधिकारों (ESCR) के अंतर्गत निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अधिकार वर्गीकृत है?

question_english: Which of the following fundamental rights is categorized under the Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights articulated in the second cluster of the UDHR (Articles 22 to 27)?
options_english: The right to equal pay for equal work without any discrimination
The right to a fair and public hearing by an independent tribunal
The right to freedom of peaceful assembly and association
The right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) The right to equal pay for equal work without any discrimination.

Detailed Justification and Typological Analysis:
1. Structure of the UDHR:
   - Articles 1–2: Fundamental principles of human dignity, liberty, equality, and non-discrimination.
   - Articles 3–21: Civil and Political Rights (First Generation Rights), including right to life, fair trial, privacy, freedom of speech, assembly, and asylum.
   - Articles 22–27: Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (Second Generation Rights), encompassing social security, right to work, health, education, and cultural participation.
   - Articles 28–30: Concluding articles on international order, duties to community, and prohibition of destructive interpretations.
2. Economic Rights in Article 23: Article 23(2) of the UDHR explicitly states: 'Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.' This is an quintessential second-generation economic right.
3. Indian Constitutional Reflection: Article 39(d) of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) mandates 'that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women', implemented statutorily via the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 and the Code on Wages, 2019.
4. Analysis of Other Options:
   - Fair and public hearing is a Civil Right under Article 10 of UDHR.
   - Freedom of peaceful assembly is a Political/Civil Right under Article 20 of UDHR.
   - Right to seek asylum is a Civil/Humanitarian Right under Article 14 of UDHR.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (a) बिना किसी भेदभाव के समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन का अधिकार।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं वर्गीकरण विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR की संरचना और अधिकारों की पीढ़ियां:
   - अनुच्छेद 1-2: मानवीय गरिमा, समानता और गैर-भेदभाव के मूल आधार।
   - अनुच्छेद 3-21: नागरिक और राजनीतिक अधिकार (प्रथम पीढ़ी के अधिकार - Civil & Political Rights), जैसे जीवन का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 3), निष्पक्ष सुनवाई (अनुच्छेद 10), शरण का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14), और शांतिपूर्ण सम्मेलन (अनुच्छेद 20)।
   - अनुच्छेद 22-27: आर्थिक, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक अधिकार (द्वितीय पीढ़ी के अधिकार - Economic, Social & Cultural Rights), जैसे सामाजिक सुरक्षा (अनुच्छेद 22), कार्य और समान वेतन का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 23), विश्राम का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 24), पर्याप्त जीवन स्तर (अनुच्छेद 25), और शिक्षा का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 26)।
2. अनुच्छेद 23(2) का प्रावधान: इसमें स्पष्ट घोषणा है कि 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को बिना किसी भेदभाव के समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन का अधिकार है।'
3. भारतीय संविधान में स्थिति: संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों के तहत अनुच्छेद 39(घ) पुरुषों और स्त्रियों दोनों के लिए 'समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन' सुनिश्चित करता है, जिसे समान पारिश्रमिक अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा कानूनी रूप दिया गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The right to equal pay for equal work

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Articles 22 through 27 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights delineate economic, social, and cultural rights essential for human dignity. Article 23 explicitly guarantees economic protections, including the right to work, free choice of employment, just working conditions, and equal pay for equal work without any form of social or gender discrimination.

question_hindi: मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) का अनुच्छेद 29 एक ऐसा मूलभूत सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित करता है जो सामूहिक कल्याण के साथ व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रताओं का संतुलन स्थापित करता है। इस अनुच्छेद में किस संकल्पना को स्पष्ट रूप से प्रतिपादित किया गया है?
options_hindi: सशस्त्र संघर्ष के दौरान मौलिक स्वतंत्रताओं का अल्पीकरण (Derogation)

question_english: Article 29 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) introduces a foundational concept that balances individual entitlements against collective welfare. What concept is explicitly enunciated in this Article?
options_english: Derogation of fundamental freedoms during armed conflict
Duties of the individual to the community
Absolute supremacy of sovereign state power
Preventive detention in the interest of national security
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) Duties of the individual to the community.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text of Article 29(1): Article 29(1) of the UDHR establishes: 'Everyone has duties to the community in which alone the free and full development of his personality is possible.'
2. Juridical Concept of Balanced Rights and Duties: Article 29 clarifies that human rights are not absolute or exercised in isolation from society. Personal liberty exists in correlation with social responsibility. Under Article 29(2), rights may be subjected to statutory limitations solely for the purpose of securing due recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others, and meeting the just requirements of morality, public order, and the general welfare in a democratic society.
3. Comparison with the Indian Constitution: This philosophy is identical to the correlation between Fundamental Rights (Part III) and Fundamental Duties under Article 51A (Part IVA) inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. As Mahatma Gandhi famously observed, rights cannot be divorced from duties, and the source of rights is duty done.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) समुदाय के प्रति व्यक्ति के कर्तव्य (Duties to the community)।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR के अनुच्छेद 29(1) का मूल पाठ: 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति का उस समुदाय के प्रति कर्तव्य है जिसमें रहकर ही उसके व्यक्तित्व का स्वतंत्र और पूर्ण विकास संभव है' (Everyone has duties to the community in which alone the free and full development of his personality is possible)।
2. अधिकारों और कर्तव्यों का संतुलन: मानवाधिकार निरपेक्ष (absolute) या समाज-निरपेक्ष नहीं हो सकते। अनुच्छेद 29(2) यह भी स्पष्ट करता है कि किसी व्यक्ति के अधिकारों पर केवल विधि द्वारा ऐसे युक्तियुक्त प्रतिबंध लगाए जा सकते हैं जो दूसरों के अधिकारों के सम्मान, सार्वजनिक व्यवस्था (Public order), नैतिकता और एक लोकतांत्रिक समाज में सामान्य कल्याण को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए आवश्यक हों।
3. भारतीय संविधान में समानांतर दर्शन: भारतीय संविधान में 42वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा जोड़े गए अनुच्छेद 51क (मौलिक कर्तव्य) इसी भावना का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। महात्मा गांधी के अनुसार भी वास्तविक अधिकारों का स्रोत कर्तव्यों के निष्ठापूर्वक पालन में निहित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Duties to the community

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights highlights that individuals have explicit duties to their community, which alone enables the free and full development of their personality. It clarifies that individual rights and freedoms can be limited by law solely to secure recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others.

question_english:
Consider the following rights:

I. Right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion
II. Right to rest, leisure, and reasonable limitation of working hours
III. Right to universal access to high-speed internet
IV. Right to an adequate standard of living for health and well-being

Which of the rights listed above are explicitly enshrined in the text of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), 1948?
options_english: I, II, and IV only
I, III, and IV only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) I, II, and IV only.

Detailed Justification and Textual Analysis:
1. Analysis of Statements:
   - Statement I: Explicitly guaranteed under Article 18 of the UDHR ('Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion...'). Corresponds to Articles 25–28 of the Indian Constitution.
   - Statement II: Explicitly guaranteed under Article 24 of the UDHR ('Everyone has the right to rest and leisure, including reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay.').
   - Statement III: The right to internet access is a modern 21st-century recognition (affirmed by UN Human Rights Council Resolution in 2016 and by the Supreme Court of India in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, 2020, under Article 19(1)(a)). However, it was NOT technologically or explicitly present in the 1948 UDHR text.
   - Statement IV: Explicitly guaranteed under Article 25(1) of the UDHR ('Everyone has the right to a standard of living adequate for the health and well-being of himself and of his family, including food, clothing, housing and medical care...'). Corresponds to Article 47 and Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
2. Conclusion: Since I, II, and IV are explicitly part of the 1948 declaration while III is not, option (a) is the only correct answer.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (a) केवल I, II और IV।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं पाठ्य विश्लेषण:
1. कथनों का परीक्षण:
   - कथन I (सही): UDHR के अनुच्छेद 18 में 'विचार, अंतरात्मा और धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार' स्पष्ट रूप से दिया गया है (भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 25 के समतुल्य)।
   - कथन II (सही): UDHR के अनुच्छेद 24 में स्पष्ट उल्लेख है कि 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को विश्राम और अवकाश का अधिकार है, जिसमें कार्य के घंटों का उचित परिसीमन और सवेतन आवधिक छुट्टियां शामिल हैं।'

   - कथन IV (सही): UDHR के अनुच्छेद 25(1) में स्पष्ट रूप से 'पर्याप्त जीवन स्तर का अधिकार' घोषित किया गया है, जिसमें भोजन, वस्त्र, आवास और चिकित्सा देखभाल शामिल है।
2. निष्कर्ष: अतः केवल I, II और IV ही UDHR (1948) में स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लिखित हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights explicitly guarantees freedom of thought, conscience, and religion in Article 18, the right to rest and leisure in Article 24, and the right to an adequate standard of living in Article 25. While digital access is recognized modernly, internet access was not explicitly included in the 1948 text.

question_hindi: मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) का अनुच्छेद 11 प्रक्रियात्मक आपराधिक न्यायशास्त्र के एक मूलभूत आधारस्तंभ को प्रतिष्ठित करता है। अनुच्छेद 11(1) के अंतर्गत सीधे तौर पर कौन-सा मौलिक सिद्धांत स्थापित किया गया है?

question_english: Article 11 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) enshrines a foundational cornerstone of procedural criminal jurisprudence. Which fundamental principle is directly established under Article 11(1)?
options_english: Absolute constitutional immunity against double jeopardy in prosecution
Presumption of innocence until proven guilty according to law
The mandatory entitlement to free legal representation at state expense
Protection against self-incrimination through custodial confessions
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) Presumption of innocence until proven guilty according to law.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text of Article 11(1) of the UDHR: 'Everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial at which he has had all the guarantees necessary for his defence.'
2. Presumption of Innocence in Criminal Jurisprudence: The presumption of innocence ('innocent until proven guilty') is the golden thread running through democratic criminal justice. The burden of proof lies entirely on the prosecution (ei incumbit probatio qui dicit, non qui negat), requiring guilt to be established beyond reasonable doubt.
3. Non-Retroactivity in Article 11(2): Article 11(2) also establishes the principle of legality (nullum crimen, nulla poena sine lege) prohibiting retroactive/ex-post facto penal laws and heavier penalties than those applicable at the time of the offence (mirrored in Article 20(1) of the Indian Constitution).
4. Related Indian Provisions:
   - Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution: Protection against double jeopardy.
   - Article 20(3) of the Indian Constitution: Protection against self-incrimination.
   - Article 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) विधि के अनुसार अपराध सिद्ध होने तक निर्दोष माने जाने की उपधारणा (Presumption of Innocence)।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR के अनुच्छेद 11(1) का मूल पाठ: 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति, जिस पर कोई दंडनीय अपराध का आरोप है, तब तक निर्दोष माना जाएगा जब तक कि उस पर ऐसी खुली अदालत में विधि अनुसार दोष सिद्ध न हो जाए, जहाँ उसे अपनी प्रतिरक्षा की सभी आवश्यक गारंटी प्राप्त रही हों।'
2. आपराधिक न्याय में महत्व: 'दोष सिद्ध होने तक निर्दोष की उपधारणा' आधुनिक आपराधिक न्याय प्रणाली का आधारभूत नियम है। इसके तहत किसी अभियुक्त पर अपराध साबित करने का भार सदैव अभियोजन पक्ष (Prosecution) पर होता है और संदेह का लाभ अभियुक्त को मिलता है।
3. अनुच्छेद 11(2) का पूरक सिद्धांत: अनुच्छेद 11(2) भूतलक्षी दांडिक विधियों (Ex-post facto laws) पर रोक लगाता है, जिसका प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 20(1) में भी मिलता है।
4. अन्य विकल्प:
   - दोहरे दंड से संरक्षण भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 20(2) में है।
   - आत्म-दोषारोपण के विरुद्ध संरक्षण अनुच्छेद 20(3) में है।
   - निःशुल्क विधिक सहायता अनुच्छेद 39क में सन्निहित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Presumption of innocence until proven guilty

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 11 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights establishes fundamental procedural fair trial guarantees in criminal law. Its primary core principle dictates that everyone charged with a penal offense is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial where they have had all the guarantees necessary for his defense.

question_hindi: एक विद्यालय के प्राचार्य को संज्ञान में आता है कि प्रशासनिक प्रवेश कार्यालय ने प्रवासी श्रमिक परिवारों के कई बच्चों को केवल इस आधार पर प्रवेश देने से मना कर दिया है कि उनके पास स्थानीय स्थायी निवास प्रमाण पत्र नहीं है। लिपिकीय निर्णय को निरस्त करते हुए, प्राचार्य उनका तत्काल नामांकन करने का आदेश देते हैं। इस प्रशासनिक निर्णय में प्राचार्य सीधे तौर पर मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) के किस मूल सिद्धांत का अनुपालन सुनिश्चित कर रहे हैं?

question_english: A school Principal discovers that the administrative admissions office has refused admission to several children belonging to migrant labor families on the sole ground that they lack local permanent residence proof. Overruling the clerical decision, the Principal orders their immediate enrollment. Which core principle of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) does the Principal directly uphold in this administrative decision?
options_english: Article 2: Universal entitlement to rights without discrimination based on status or origin
Article 13: Freedom of movement and residence within the borders of each state
Article 23: Right to work and free choice of employment
Article 17: Right to own property and freedom from arbitrary deprivation
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) Article 2: Universal entitlement to rights without discrimination based on status or origin.

Detailed Justification and Administrative/Legal Analysis:
1. UDHR Article 2 (Non-Discrimination Principle): Article 2 provides: 'Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.' Denying migrant children educational access based on lack of domicile paperwork creates discriminatory exclusion based on economic and social status/birth origin.
2. Intersection with Article 26 (Right to Education): Article 26 guarantees elementary education as compulsory and free. By eliminating artificial bureaucratic barriers to education for vulnerable migrant children, the Principal operationalizes Article 2 read with Article 26 of the UDHR.
3. Indian Statutory Framework (RTE Act, 2009):
   - Section 15 of the RTE Act explicitly specifies that a child shall be admitted in a school at the commencement of the academic year or within such extended period as may be prescribed.
   - No child can be denied admission for lack of age proof, residence proof, or transfer certificate. The Ministry of Education guidelines and Supreme Court directives mandate that children of seasonal migrant workers must be enrolled without demanding local residential certificates.
4. Relevant Child Rights Conventions: Article 2 and Article 28 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC, 1989), ratified by India in 1992, similarly mandate non-discrimination and free compulsory primary schooling for all children within the state's jurisdiction.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (a) अनुच्छेद 2: सामाजिक मूल अथवा प्रस्थिति के आधार पर बिना किसी भेदभाव के अधिकारों की सार्वभौमिक हकदारी।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं प्रशासनिक/विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR का अनुच्छेद 2 (विभेद का प्रतिषेध): अनुच्छेद 2 घोषित करता है कि 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति इस घोषणा में उल्लिखित सभी अधिकारों और स्वतंत्रताओं का बिना किसी भेद के हकदार है, चाहे वह नस्ल, रंग, लिंग, भाषा, धर्म, राजनीतिक विचार, राष्ट्रीय या सामाजिक मूल, संपत्ति, जन्म या अन्य किसी प्रस्थिति (status) पर आधारित हो।'
2. शिक्षा के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 26) के साथ अंतर्संबंध: प्रवासी श्रमिकों के बच्चों को केवल निवास प्रमाण पत्र के अभाव में शिक्षा से वंचित करना उनकी सामाजिक-आर्थिक स्थिति के आधार पर भेदभाव है। प्राचार्य का हस्तक्षेप यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि प्रशासनिक प्रक्रियाएं वंचित वर्गों के मौलिक मानवाधिकारों के आड़े न आएं।
3. भारतीय विधिक ढांचा (RTE अधिनियम, 2009): बच्चों का निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम (RTE Act), 2009 की धारा 15 और इसके नियम स्पष्ट करते हैं कि किसी भी बच्चे को जन्म प्रमाण पत्र, पते के प्रमाण अथवा स्थानांतरण प्रमाण पत्र (TC) के अभाव में प्रवेश से वंचित नहीं किया जा सकता। शिक्षा मंत्रालय के दिशानिर्देशों के तहत प्रवासी बच्चों को तुरंत नामांकित कर विशेष प्रशिक्षण प्रदान करने का दायित्व विद्यालय प्रमुख का होता है।
4. बाल अधिकारों पर अभिसमय (UNCRC, 1989): भारत द्वारा 1992 में अनुसमर्थित UNCRC का अनुच्छेद 2 और 28 भी प्रत्येक बच्चे के लिए बिना भेदभाव के शिक्षा की गारंटी देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Article 2: Non-discrimination in the enjoyment of rights

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 2 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights establishes the core principle of non-discrimination, entitling every individual to all human rights regardless of background. Admitting migrant children despite administrative paperwork deficiencies directly upholds this non-discriminatory guarantee, ensuring social or economic origin does not restrict access to fundamental educational rights.

question_english: Under the provisions of the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, who among the following is eligible for appointment as the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?

A person who has been a Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court
Any sitting or retired Chief Justice of a High Court in India
An eminent jurist nominated directly by the President of India
explanation_english: Under Section 3(2)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, prior to the 2019 amendment, only a person who had been a Chief Justice of India was eligible to be appointed as the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC). However, finding eligible and willing retired Chief Justices of India frequently proved difficult, leading to delays and vacancies. To resolve this institutional bottleneck, Parliament enacted the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 33 of 2019), which amended Section 3(2)(a) to provide that the Chairperson shall be a person who has been a Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court. This amendment widened the pool of judicial talent available for heading the apex human rights watchdog while retaining supreme judicial expertise at the helm.
explanation_hindi: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 3(2)(क) के मूल प्रावधानों के अनुसार, केवल वही व्यक्ति राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) का अध्यक्ष नियुक्त होने का पात्र था जो भारत का मुख्य न्यायाधीश (Chief Justice of India) रहा हो। हालांकि, सेवानिवृत्त मुख्य न्यायाधीशों की सीमित उपलब्धता और पद रिक्त रहने की समस्याओं को दूर करने के उद्देश्य से संसद द्वारा मानव अधिकार संरक्षण (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 पारित किया गया। इस संशोधन के माध्यम से धारा 3(2)(क) में संशोधन कर यह व्यवस्था की गई कि अब वह व्यक्ति जो भारत का मुख्य न्यायाधीश रहा हो या उच्चतम न्यायालय का न्यायाधीश रहा हो, आयोग के अध्यक्ष पद हेतु पात्र होगा। इससे आयोग के शीर्ष पद पर चयन का दायरा व्यापक हुआ है तथा न्यायिक विशेषज्ञता भी सुरक्षित रही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) A person who has been a Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Following the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act of 2019, the eligibility criteria for the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission were expanded. question_english: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) includes several ex-officio members heading various statutory bodies. Which of the following commissions was added to the NHRC as an ex-officio member by the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019?
options_english: The National Commission for Minorities
The National Commission for Women
The National Commission for Backward Classes
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
explanation_english: Under Section 3(3) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and the National Commission for Women were designated as ex-officio members of the NHRC. The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 significantly widened this institutional representation by adding three new categories of ex-officio members: (1) the Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), established as a constitutional body under Article 338B via the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018; (2) the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005; and (3) the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, appointed under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Among the given options, the National Commission for Backward Classes is the one added by the 2019 amendment.

question_english: Under the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, how many members having specialized knowledge of, or practical experience in, matters relating to human rights are appointed to the National Human Rights Commission?
options_english: Two members, out of which at least one shall be a woman
Three members, out of which at least one shall be a woman
Four members, representing different geographical zones of India
Five members, out of which at least two shall be women
explanation_english: Under the original Section 3(2)(d) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, two members were appointed from amongst persons having knowledge of, or practical experience in, matters relating to human rights, with no statutory reservation or mandate regarding gender representation. The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 amended Section 3(2)(d) to increase the number of these non-judicial expert members from two to three, and introduced a mandatory statutory requirement that at least one of these three members must be a woman. This structural change ensures gender diversity and strengthens civil society and gender-sensitive perspectives in the adjudication and investigation of human rights issues.
explanation_hindi: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 3(2)(घ) के मूल प्रावधान के अनुसार, मानव अधिकारों के क्षेत्र में विशेष ज्ञान अथवा व्यावहारिक अनुभव रखने वाले 2 सदस्यों की नियुक्ति का प्रावधान था, जिसमें महिलाओं के अनिवार्य प्रतिनिधित्व का कोई वैधानिक उल्लेख नहीं था। मानव अधिकार संरक्षण (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा इस व्यवस्था में महत्वपूर्ण सुधार किया गया। अब इन विशेषज्ञ सदस्यों की संख्या 2 से बढ़ाकर 3 कर दी गई है तथा यह अनिवार्य शर्त जोड़ी गई है कि इन तीन सदस्यों में से कम से कम एक सदस्य 'महिला' अवश्य होनी चाहिए। इस संशोधन का उद्देश्य आयोग में लैंगिक विविधता तथा संवेदनशीलता सुनिश्चित करना है।

question_english: The Chairperson and Members of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) are appointed by the President of India on the recommendations of a high-powered selection committee. Who among the following is NOT a member of this selection committee?
options_english: The Prime Minister
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha (House of the People)
The Union Minister of Home Affairs
The Chief Justice of India
explanation_english: Under Section 4(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the Chairperson and Members of the NHRC are appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal, upon the recommendation of a six-member committee consisting of: (1) The Prime Minister (who acts as the Chairperson of the Committee); (2) The Speaker of the House of the People (Lok Sabha); (3) The Minister in-charge of the Ministry of Home Affairs in the Government of India; (4) The Leader of the Opposition in the House of the People; (5) The Leader of the Opposition in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); and (6) The Deputy Chairman of the Council of States. The Chief Justice of India is NOT a member of this committee. However, the first proviso to Section 4(1) mandates that no sitting Judge of the Supreme Court or sitting Chief Justice of a High Court shall be appointed except after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
explanation_hindi: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 4(1) के अनुसार, राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग के अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा अपने हस्ताक्षर और मुद्रा युक्त अधिपत्र द्वारा 6-सदस्यीय उच्चाधिकार प्राप्त चयन समिति की सिफारिशों के आधार पर की जाती है। इस चयन समिति में निम्नलिखित शामिल होते हैं: (1) प्रधान मंत्री (समिति के अध्यक्ष), (2) लोकसभा अध्यक्ष, (3) केंद्रीय गृह मंत्री, (4) लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता, (5) राज्यसभा में विपक्ष के नेता, तथा (6) राज्यसभा के उपसभापति। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) इस चयन समिति के सदस्य नहीं होते हैं। यद्यपि, धारा 4(1) के परंतुक के अनुसार यदि किसी आसीन (sitting) उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश या उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश को नियुक्त करना हो, तो भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश से परामर्श आवश्यक होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The Chief Justice of India

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 4 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a six-member selection committee. This committee includes the Prime Minister, House Speaker, Union Home Minister, Opposition Leaders, and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, excluding the Chief Justice.

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition, tenure, and eligibility criteria of the NHRC following the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019:
I. The tenure of office for the Chairperson and Members is three years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
II. Both the Chairperson and Members are eligible for re-appointment.
III. A person who is or has been a Chief Justice of a High Court is eligible for appointment as a Member of the Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
explanation_english:
All three statements are correct under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, as amended in 2019:
1. Statement I is correct: Section 6(1) and 6(3) were amended by the 2019 Amendment Act to reduce the term of office of the Chairperson and Members of the NHRC from 5 years to 3 years, or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
2. Statement II is correct: Prior to 2019, there was a restriction that prevented re-appointment after a second 5-year term or restricted Chairperson re-appointment. The 2019 amendment amended Section 6(1) and Section 6(3) to expressly provide that a person appointed as Chairperson or Member shall be eligible for re-appointment (subject to the 70-year age cap).
3. Statement III is correct: Under Section 3(2)(c) of the Act, one Member of the Commission is appointed who is, or has been, a Chief Justice of a High Court (along with one Member who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court under Section 3(2)(b)).
Therefore, statements I, II, and III are all correct.
explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 के परिप्रेक्ष्य में तीनों कथन पूर्णतः सही हैं:
1. कथन I सही है: 2019 के संशोधन द्वारा अधिनियम की धारा 6 में संशोधन करके अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों के कार्यकाल को 5 वर्ष से घटाकर 3 वर्ष या 70 वर्ष की आयु (जो भी पहले हो) कर दिया गया है।
2. कथन II सही है: 2019 के संशोधन से पूर्व अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों की पुनर्नियुक्ति पर कड़े प्रतिबंध थे। 2019 के संशोधन के तहत धारा 6 में यह प्रावधान किया गया कि अध्यक्ष और सदस्य पुनर्नियुक्ति (Re-appointment) के लिए पात्र होंगे (70 वर्ष की अधिकतम आयु सीमा के अधीन)।
3. कथन III सही है: अधिनियम की धारा 3(2)(ग) के अंतर्गत आयोग में एक ऐसा सदस्य नियुक्त किया जाता है जो किसी उच्च न्यायालय का मुख्य न्यायाधीश रहा हो या है (तथा धारा 3(2)(ख) के तहत एक सदस्य जो उच्चतम न्यायालय का न्यायाधीश रहा हो या है)।
अतः विकल्प (D) अर्थात् 'I, II और III' सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 2019 amendment reduced the tenure of the Chairperson and Members of the National Human Rights Commission from five years to three years, or until reaching 70 years of age. Furthermore, it made them eligible for re- appointment and permitted former High Court Chief Justices to be appointed as Members of the Commission.

A is false, but R is true
explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: The NHRC is characterized as a quasi-judicial body because under Section 13 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, while inquiring into complaints of human rights violations, it possesses all the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (such as summoning and enforcing the attendance of witnesses, examining them on oath, discovery and production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits). Furthermore, its proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings within the meaning of Sections 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
Reason (R) is false: The NHRC does not possess the power of a regular court of law to deliver binding judgments, convict individuals, or impose criminal punishments or prison sentences. Under Section 18 of the PHRA, its findings and recommendations are advisory in nature. It recommends prosecution, compensation, or immediate interim relief to the concerned government or authority, or approaches the Supreme Court or High Court for necessary directions. Thus, A is true but R is false.
explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सही है: राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) एक अर्ध-न्यायिक (Quasi-judicial) निकाय है क्योंकि मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 13 के तहत शिकायतों की जाँच करते समय इसे सिविल प्रक्रिया संहिता, 1908 (CPC) के अंतर्गत एक दीवानी अदालत (Civil Court) की सभी शक्तियाँ प्राप्त हैं (जैसे साक्षियों को समन जारी करना, शपथ पर परीक्षण करना, दस्तावेज मंगाना तथा हलफनामे पर साक्ष्य प्राप्त करना)। इसके अलावा, धारा 13(4) के तहत इसकी कार्यवाहियों को भारतीय दंड संहिता (IPC) की धारा 193 और 228 के तहत न्यायिक कार्यवाही माना जाता है।
कारण (R) गलत है: NHRC के पास नियमित न्यायालयों की तरह बाध्यकारी निर्णय सुनाने या दोषियों को आपराधिक सजा (कारावास/दंड) देने का कोई अधिकार नहीं है। धारा 18 के अनुसार आयोग की भूमिका मुख्य रूप से सिफारिशी/सलाहकारी (advisory/recommendatory) है; यह संबंधित सरकार या प्राधिकरण को अभियोजन शुरू करने, मुआवजा देने या अंतरिम राहत प्रदान करने की केवल सिफारिश कर सकता है। अतः A सही है, लेकिन R गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A is true but R is false

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The National Human Rights Commission functions as a quasi-judicial body empowered to investigate complaints, summon witnesses, and examine evidence under civil court procedures. However, it cannot render binding judicial sentences or criminal punishments directly, as its legal recommendations must be submitted to appropriate government authorities for enforcement, rendering the reason false.

question_english: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 expanded the ex-officio membership of the NHRC to include the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities. Which of the following officials was also added as an ex-officio member under the same amendment?
options_english: Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal (NGT)
Chief Information Commissioner of the Central Information Commission (CIC)
Chairperson of the University Grants Commission (UGC)
explanation_english:
Prior to 2019, Section 3(3) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 provided ex-officio status only to the Chairpersons of four statutory commissions: National Commission for Minorities, National Commission for Scheduled Castes, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and National Commission for Women. The 2019 Amendment Act broadened the mandate of the NHRC to encompass vulnerable sections such as children, backward classes, and persons with disabilities. Specifically, it amended Section 3(3) to include:
1. The Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (constituted under Section 3 of the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005);
2. The Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes; and
3. The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (appointed under Section 74(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016).
Therefore, the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is the official added alongside the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Chairperson, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act of 2019 substantially broadened ex-officio representation within the National Human Rights Commission. Alongside the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, it added the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights as an ex-officio member to strengthen structural protection for vulnerable youth across India.

question_english: In what manner can the Chairperson or any Member of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) be removed from office on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity?
options_english: By an order of the President of India, following an inquiry and report by the Supreme Court
By a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament (impeachment)
By the Prime Minister on the binding recommendation of the Union Cabinet
By the Chief Justice of India following an internal judicial committee inquiry
explanation_english:
Under Section 5(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson or any Member of the NHRC can only be removed from office by order of the President of India on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. However, the President can issue such an order only after the Supreme Court, on a reference being made to it by the President, has held an inquiry in accordance with the prescribed procedure and reported that the Chairperson or Member ought on any such ground to be removed.
Additionally, under Section 5(2), the President may remove the Chairperson or any Member without a Supreme Court inquiry if that person is adjudged an insolvent, engages in paid employment outside the duties of the office during their term, is unfit to continue by reason of infirmity of mind or body, is of unsound mind declared by a competent court, or is convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for an offense involving moral turpitude.
explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 5(1) के अनुसार, राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग के अध्यक्ष या किसी सदस्य को साबित कदाचार या असमर्थता के आधार पर केवल राष्ट्रपति के आदेश द्वारा ही हटाया जा सकता है। परंतु ऐसा आदेश राष्ट्रपति केवल तभी जारी कर सकते हैं जब राष्ट्रपति द्वारा इस संदर्भ में मामला भेजे जाने पर उच्चतम न्यायालय (Supreme Court) द्वारा निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के अनुसार औपचारिक जाँच की गई हो और उच्चतम न्यायालय ने अपनी रिपोर्ट में संबंधित व्यक्ति को हटाए जाने की अनुशंसा की हो।
इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 5(2) के तहत कुछ विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों (जैसे दिवालिया घोषित होना, मानसिक या शारीरिक रूप से अस्वस्थ होना, अपने पद के कर्तव्यों से इतर कोई सवेतन नियोजन करना, या नैतिक अधमता वाले अपराध में सिद्धदोष ठहराया जाना) में राष्ट्रपति सीधे भी पदमुक्त कर सकते हैं। अतः साबित कदाचार या असमर्थता के मामले में उच्चतम न्यायालय की जाँच अनिवार्य है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) By an order of the President, passed after an inquiry by the Supreme Court

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 5 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Chairperson or any Member of the Commission can only be removed from office by an order of the President of India. Such removal requires a formal inquiry conducted by the Supreme Court, which must report proved misbehavior or incapacity following due process.

question_english: Who serves as the chief executive officer and administrative head of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), responsible for implementing the decisions and administrative affairs of the Commission?
options_english: The Chairperson of the Commission
The Secretary-General
The Director General of Investigation
The Registrar (Law)
explanation_english: Under Section 3(4) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, there is a Secretary-General who is the Chief Executive Officer of the Commission and exercises such powers and discharges such functions of the Commission (other than judicial functions and the power to make regulations under Section 40B) as may be delegated by the Commission or the Chairperson. The 2019 amendment further clarified that the Secretary-General exercises all administrative and financial powers (except judicial functions and regulation-making powers). While the Chairperson is the institutional head and guides the policy and judicial functioning, the Secretary-General (an officer of the rank of Secretary to the Government of India) functions as the administrative head responsible for day-to-day administrative machinery and executive implementation.
explanation_hindi: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 3(4) के अनुसार, आयोग का एक महासचिव (Secretary-General) होता है, जो आयोग का मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी (Chief Executive Officer) होता है। मानव अधिकार संरक्षण (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा धारा 3(4) को और अधिक स्पष्ट करते हुए यह निर्धारित किया गया कि महासचिव न्यायिक कार्यों तथा धारा 40B के अधीन विनियम बनाने की शक्ति को छोड़कर, आयोग की समस्त प्रशासनिक और वित्तीय शक्तियों (Administrative and Financial Powers) का प्रयोग करेगा। यद्यपि अध्यक्ष आयोग के सर्वोच्च नीतिगत एवं न्यायिक प्रमुख होते हैं, परंतु दैनिक प्रशासनिक कार्यों, सचिवालय के नियंत्रण और आयोग के निर्णयों के प्रशासनिक निष्पादन का दायित्व भारत सरकार के सचिव स्तर के अधिकारी यानी महासचिव पर होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The Secretary-General

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Secretary-General serves as the chief administrative officer of the National Human Rights Commission. Exercising administrative and financial powers delegated by the Commission, the Secretary-General oversees daily operations, directs administrative divisions, manages organizational personnel, and ensures the effective execution and implementation of all decisions, investigations, and policy mandates passed by the Commission.

question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The statutory composition of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) mandates the inclusion of members with prior judicial experience from the higher judiciary.
Reason (R): Inquiring into allegations of human rights violations often entails complex interpretations of constitutional provisions, statutory laws, and procedural fairness, necessitating rigorous judicial training to assess evidence.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Section 3(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson must be a former Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court, one member must be or have been a Judge of the Supreme Court, and one member must be or have been the Chief Justice of a High Court. Thus, the statutory framework explicitly mandates the inclusion of judges with high judicial standing.
Reason (R) is true: The NHRC inquires into grave human rights violations, custodial violence, fake encounters, arbitrary detentions, and denial of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19, 21, and 22 of the Constitution of India. These inquiries require understanding complex criminal and constitutional law, evaluating evidentiary reliability, exercising powers equivalent to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, and balancing state authority with individual liberties. Because judicial training is essential to carry out these quasi-judicial investigative duties impartially and accurately, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सही है: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 3(2) के अनुसार, आयोग के अध्यक्ष (भूतपूर्व CJI या उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश), एक सदस्य (उच्चतम न्यायालय के आसीन या सेवानिवृत्त न्यायाधीश), तथा एक अन्य सदस्य (किसी उच्च न्यायालय के आसीन या सेवानिवृत्त मुख्य न्यायाधीश) का न्यायिक पृष्ठभूमि से होना अनिवार्य है।
कारण (R) भी सही है: मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनों की जाँच में हिरासत में हिंसा, फर्जी मुठभेड़, गैर-कानूनी गिरफ्तारी तथा संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14, 19, 21 और 22 के तहत प्रदत्त मौलिक अधिकारों के हनन से जुड़े अत्यंत जटिल संवैधानिक एवं विधिक प्रश्न शामिल होते हैं। ऐसी शिकायतों के निष्पक्ष परीक्षण, सिविल प्रक्रिया संहिता के तहत साक्ष्य जुटाने और राज्य की जवाबदेही तय करने के लिए गहन न्यायिक समझ और प्रशिक्षण की अनिवार्य आवश्यकता होती है। अतः कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या प्रस्तुत करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The statutory composition of the National Human Rights Commission explicitly requires members with judicial backgrounds from the Supreme Court and High Courts. Judicial expertise is essential because human rights inquiries demand rigorous evaluation of legal evidence, constitutional statutory interpretations, procedural fairness, and objective assessment of state accountability during complex human rights investigations.

question_english: A school Principal receives a formal notice from the NHRC requesting an inquiry report regarding an alleged incident of severe corporal punishment inflicted on a student six months ago. The Principal ignores the notice, assuming the NHRC lacks coercive authority. Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what legal course of action can the NHRC initiate?
options_english: The NHRC can issue an arrest warrant against the Principal for contempt of proceedings
The NHRC can issue summons requiring personal attendance and examine the Principal on oath
The NHRC can issue a binding executive order to immediately dismiss the Principal from service
The NHRC has no coercive legal powers and can only issue repeated administrative reminders
explanation_english: Corporal punishment in schools constitutes a direct violation of a child's fundamental right to life, dignity, and bodily integrity under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, and is prohibited under Section 17 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. When the NHRC inquires into such human rights violations, it is equipped under Section 13(1)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 with the powers of a civil court to summon and enforce the attendance of any person (including school administrators and public officials) and examine them on oath. If an official refuses or neglects to comply with the Commission's requisition or summons, they are liable under Sections 175, 178, 179, and 180 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and the Commission can forward the case to a magistrate having jurisdiction under Section 345 and Section 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The NHRC cannot directly dismiss the Principal or issue an immediate arrest warrant for contempt on its own, but it has the statutory power to summon and examine the Principal on oath.
explanation_hindi: विद्यालयों में बच्चों को शारीरिक या मानसिक प्रताड़ना देना संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत गरिमापूर्ण जीवन के अधिकार का उल्लंघन है तथा शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 17 के तहत दंडनीय है। जब NHRC ऐसे मानव अधिकार हनन के मामलों की जाँच करता है, तो मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 13(1)(क) के अंतर्गत उसे किसी भी व्यक्ति को समन (Summons) जारी करने, उसकी व्यक्तिगत उपस्थिति बाध्यकारी बनाने तथा शपथ पर उसकी परीक्षा (examine on oath) करने की दीवानी न्यायालय की पूर्ण शक्ति प्राप्त होती है। यदि कोई प्राधिकारी या संस्था प्रमुख जानबूझकर आयोग के नोटिस की अवहेलना करता है, तो आयोग समन जारी कर उसे व्यक्तिगत रूप से तलब कर सकता है। आयोग सीधे किसी कर्मचारी को बर्खास्त नहीं कर सकता और न ही स्वतः गिरफ्तारी वारंट निकाल सकता है, लेकिन समन और शपथ पर बयान लेने की विधिक शक्ति से अनुपालन सुनिश्चित कराता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The NHRC can summon and examine the Principal on oath.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 13 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Commission possesses civil court powers to compel attendance and enforce legal cooperation. If an institutional administrator ignores formal inquiries, the Commission can issue binding summons, require document production, and examine the administrator on oath, making non-compliance legally punishable under civil judicial procedures.

question_english: Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 prescribes a special procedure regarding complaints alleging human rights violations by members of the Armed Forces. What is the statutory limitation imposed on the NHRC in such cases?
options_english: The NHRC is completely barred from taking cognizance and must dismiss the petition outright
The NHRC can conduct independent field investigations using its own investigation team
The NHRC may only call for a report from the Central Government and make recommendations based on that report
The NHRC can investigate armed forces personnel only upon a direct reference from the President of India
explanation_english:
Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 sets forth a special and restrictive procedure dealing with human rights violations alleged to have been committed by members of the Armed Forces (defined under Section 2(1)(a) to include naval, military, and air forces, as well as any other armed forces of the Union).
Under Section 19(1):
(a) The Commission cannot deploy its own investigative team or summon armed forces personnel directly; it may, either on its own motion or on a petition, seek a report from the Central Government.
(b) After the receipt of the report, it may either not proceed with the complaint or, as the case may be, make its recommendations to that Government.
Under Section 19(2), the Central Government is required to inform the Commission of the action taken within three months (or extended time). Under Section 19(3), the Commission must publish its report along with its recommendations and the government's action. Hence, the Commission's power is limited to calling for a report from the Central Government and making recommendations.
explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 19 सशस्त्र बलों (थल सेना, नौसेना, वायु सेना और संघ के अन्य सशस्त्र बल) द्वारा किए गए कथित मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनों के मामलों में आयोग की शक्तियों को सीमित करती है। इस धारा के अंतर्गत:
1. NHRC स्वयं अपनी अन्वेषण विंग के माध्यम से सशस्त्र बलों के विरुद्ध प्रत्यक्ष स्वतंत्र जमीनी जाँच नहीं कर सकता।
2. धारा 19(1)(क) के तहत आयोग स्वप्रेरणा से या याचिका पर 'केंद्र सरकार से एक रिपोर्ट' (seek a report from the Central Government) मांग सकता है।
3. रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होने के बाद, धारा 19(1)(ख) के तहत आयोग मामले को समाप्त कर सकता है अथवा केंद्र सरकार को अपनी सिफारिशें (recommendations) भेज सकता है।
केंद्र सरकार को 3 माह के भीतर की गई कार्रवाई की जानकारी आयोग को देनी होती है, जिसे आयोग सार्वजनिक करता है। अतः आयोग की शक्ति केवल केंद्र सरकार से रिपोर्ट मांगने और उस पर अपनी सिफारिशें देने तक सीमित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) It may only seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act outlines a specialized procedure regarding alleged violations committed by members of the Armed Forces. The Commission cannot conduct independent direct investigations into military personnel; instead, it may seek a report from the Central Government and subsequently make non-binding recommendations or reports based on that information.

question_english: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what is the statutory period of limitation barring the National Human Rights Commission from inquiring into a human rights violation?
options_english: The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of six months from the date of the incident
The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the violation is alleged to have been committed
The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of three years from the date of the incident
There is no period of limitation; human rights violations can be inquired into at any time
explanation_english:
Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 lays down a strict bar on the jurisdiction of the Commission with respect to older complaints: 'The Commission or the State Commission shall not inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.'
This one-year limitation period is designed to prevent stale claims, ensure prompt reporting and swift investigation while evidence remains fresh and witnesses are accessible. However, if a violation is of a continuing nature (continuing wrong), the limitation clock may run from the last date of such continued violation as interpreted by judicial precedents.
explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 36(2) के अंतर्गत आयोग के अधिकार क्षेत्र पर एक स्पष्ट वैधानिक समय-सीमा (Limitation Period) लगाई गई है। इस उपधारा के अनुसार: 'आयोग या राज्य आयोग ऐसे किसी मामले की जाँच नहीं करेगा जो उस तारीख से एक वर्ष (one year) की समाप्ति के बाद प्रस्तुत किया गया हो जिस तारीख को मानव अधिकारों के उल्लंघन का कथित कृत्य किया गया था।'
इस प्रावधान का उद्देश्य शिकायतों की शीघ्र रिपोर्टिंग को प्रोत्साहित करना, बासी मामलों (stale claims) से बचना तथा साक्ष्यों और गवाहों की प्रामाणिकता बनी रहने के दौरान त्वरित जाँच सुनिश्चित करना है। अतः घटना की तिथि से 1 वर्ष बीत जाने के बाद NHRC मामले की जाँच नहीं कर सकता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 imposes a strict statutory limitation period on the Commission’s jurisdiction. The National Human Rights Commission is legally barred from inquiring into any human rights violation complaint if it is submitted after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged incident.

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the statutory functions and powers of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
I. It can intervene in any legal proceeding involving allegations of human rights violations pending before a court, subject to the approval of such court.
II. It can visit any jail or other custodial institution under the control of a State Government to inspect the living conditions of the inmates.
III. It can review constitutional and legal safeguards for the protection of human rights and recommend measures for their effective implementation.
IV. It can directly impose financial penalties and levy fines on State Governments that fail to implement its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
explanation_english:
Under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993:
- Statement I is correct: Under Section 12(b), the NHRC has the power to intervene in any proceeding involving any allegation of violation of human rights pending before a court, with the approval of such court.
- Statement II is correct: Under Section 12(c), the NHRC can visit, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, any jail or other institution under the control of the State Government, where persons are detained or lodged, to study the living conditions of the inmates and make recommendations thereon.
- Statement III is correct: Under Section 12(d), the Commission can review the safeguards provided by or under the Constitution or any law for the time being in force for the protection of human rights and recommend measures for their effective implementation.
- Statement IV is incorrect: The NHRC has no statutory power to adjudicate criminal penalties, levy fines, or directly enforce financial penalties against State Governments. Its recommendations under Section 18 are advisory, though State authorities are required to submit action taken reports or reasons for non-compliance, and the Commission can approach the High Courts or the Supreme Court for appropriate writs and enforcement.
Therefore, only statements I, II, and III are correct.
explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 12 के अंतर्गत आयोग के कार्यों का विस्तृत विवरण दिया गया है:
- कथन I सही है: धारा 12(ख) के अनुसार, आयोग किसी न्यायालय की अनुमति से उस न्यायालय के समक्ष लंबित मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन से जुड़ी किसी भी कार्यवाही में हस्तक्षेप (intervene) कर सकता है।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 12(ग) के तहत आयोग बंदियों की रहन-सहन की दशाओं का अध्ययन करने और सुधार के उपाय सुझाने के लिए राज्य सरकार के नियंत्रणाधीन किसी जेल, हिरासत केंद्र या अन्य सुधार गृह का दौरा कर सकता है।
- कथन III सही है: धारा 12(घ) के तहत आयोग संविधान या किसी अन्य कानून के तहत मानव अधिकारों के संरक्षण के लिए उपलब्ध उपायों व सुरक्षा प्रावधानों की समीक्षा कर सकता है और उनके प्रभावी क्रियान्वयन की सिफारिश कर सकता है।
- कथन IV गलत है: NHRC के पास राज्य सरकारों पर सीधे वित्तीय जुर्माना (Financial Penalties) लगाने या दंडात्मक आदेश पारित करने की कोई वैधानिक शक्ति नहीं है। धारा 18 के अंतर्गत आयोग के निष्कर्ष और सिफारिशें सलाहकारी प्रकृति की होती हैं, यद्यपि अनुपालन न होने पर आयोग उच्च न्यायालय या उच्चतम न्यायालय में याचिका दायर कर सकता है।
अतः केवल कथन I, II और III सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Commission is authorized to intervene in judicial proceedings involving human rights with court approval, visit custodial institutions to inspect living conditions, and review constitutional protections. However, it lacks statutory authority to impose direct financial penalties on state governments for non- compliance.

question_hindi: किसी लोक सेवक (public servant) द्वारा मानव अधिकारों के उल्लंघन अथवा ऐसे उल्लंघन के निवारण में घोर उपेक्षा की पुष्टि करने वाली जांच पूरी होने पर, राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 के अंतर्गत क्या कार्रवाई कर सकता है?

question_english: Upon concluding an inquiry that establishes a violation of human rights or negligence in the prevention of human rights violations by a public servant, what action is the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) empowered to take under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
options_english: It can directly initiate internal departmental disciplinary proceedings and impose penalties on the public servant.
It can directly register a First Information Report (FIR) and prosecute the errant public servant in a criminal court.
Recommend that the concerned Government or authority initiate prosecution or suitable disciplinary action against the public servant.
It can pass a legally binding judicial order for the immediate demotion or dismissal of the public servant.
explanation_english:
Under Section 18 of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) functions essentially as an inquiry, oversight, and recommendatory body rather than a punitive judicial tribunal or enforcement agency.
Key statutory provisions under Section 18 include:
1. Recommendatory Powers: Where the inquiry discloses the commission of a human rights violation or negligence in its prevention by a public servant, the Commission may recommend to the concerned Government or authority the initiation of proceedings for prosecution or other suitable disciplinary action against the concerned person (Section 18(a)(ii)).
2. Immediate Interim Relief: Under Section 18(a)(i), the Commission can recommend the grant of immediate interim relief to the victim or their family members.
3. Constitutional Remedies: Under Section 18(b), the NHRC can approach the Supreme Court (under Article 32) or the High Court (under Article 226) for directions, orders, or writs.
4. Absence of Direct Punitive Authority: The NHRC cannot directly convict, fine, penalize, demote, dismiss, or register an FIR against errant public servants. It forwards its findings to the government, which must submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within one month.
5. Constitutional Separation of Powers: This framework upholds Article 50 (Separation of Judiciary from Executive), ensuring that investigative recommendations do not usurp judicial or executive disciplinary prerogatives.
explanation_hindi:
मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 18 के तहत राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) मुख्य रूप से एक जांच, निगरानी और अनुशंसात्मक (recommendatory) निकाय के रूप में कार्य करता है, न कि प्रत्यक्ष दंडात्मक या न्यायिक प्राधिकरण के रूप में।
धारा 18 के प्रमुख कानूनी प्रावधान एवं बिंदु:
1. अनुशंसा की शक्ति: जब धारा 13 के अधीन की गई जांच से यह सिद्ध होता है कि किसी लोक सेवक द्वारा मानवाधिकारों का उल्लंघन किया गया है या उसके निवारण में उपेक्षा बरती गई है, तो आयोग संबंधित सरकार या सक्षम प्राधिकारी से संबंधित व्यक्ति के विरुद्ध अभियोजन चलाने या उपयुक्त अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई शुरू करने की सिफारिश कर सकता है [धारा 18(क)(ii)]।
2. तत्काल अंतरिम राहत: धारा 18(क)(i) के तहत, आयोग पीड़ित या उसके परिजनों को तत्काल अंतरिम वित्तीय अथवा मानवीय सहायता देने की सिफारिश कर सकता है।
3. उच्चतर न्यायालयों में जाने का अधिकार: धारा 18(ख) के तहत, आयोग उचित आदेशों या रिटों हेतु सीधे उच्चतम न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 32) या उच्च न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 226) में याचिका प्रस्तुत कर सकता है।
4. प्रत्यक्ष दंडात्मक शक्तियों का अभाव: एनएचआरसी किसी लोक सेवक को सीधे बर्खास्त, पदावनत या दंडित नहीं कर सकता, न ही वह स्वयं एफआईआर दर्ज कर मुकदमा चला सकता है। संबंधित सरकार को एक माह के भीतर उस पर की गई कार्रवाई की रिपोर्ट (ATR) आयोग को प्रस्तुत करनी होती है।
5. संवैधानिक शक्ति संतुलन: यह व्यवस्था कार्यपालिका, न्यायपालिका और सांविधिक आयोगों के बीच शक्ति संतुलन (Separation of Powers) बनाए रखने हेतु बनाई गई है।

explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the direct and correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Detailed Institutional Analysis:
1. The "Toothless Tiger" Critique: Former Chief Justice of India and NHRC Chairperson H.L. Dattu publicly acknowledged that the Commission functions like a "toothless tiger". While it commands broad investigative powers, its remedial outputs are non-binding recommendations.
2. Advisory Nature (Section 18): Under Section 18 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Commission can only "recommend" to the concerned government or authority to initiate prosecution, pay interim relief, or take departmental action. The government is obliged only to examine the report and communicate an Action Taken Report (ATR) within one month. If the government rejects or fails to implement the recommendations, the NHRC possesses no contempt powers or enforcement mechanisms to compel compliance.
3. Jurisdictional Limitations: Furthermore, under Section 19, its powers regarding armed forces are limited to seeking a report from the Central Government, and under Section 36(2), it cannot inquire into matters after the expiry of one year from the date of the incident. These statutory limitations directly justify why it is labeled a toothless tiger.

question_english: Does the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) have the statutory mandate to study international treaties and other international instruments on human rights and make recommendations for their effective domestic implementation?

explanation_english:
Under Section 12(f) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the Commission is explicitly tasked with the function to "study treaties and other international instruments on human rights and make recommendations for their effective implementation."
Key Aspects of Section 12:
1. Statutory Charter of Functions: Section 12 outlines the core responsibilities of the NHRC, including suo motu and petitioned inquiries (Section 12(a)), jail visits (Section 12(c)), constitutional and legal reviews (Section 12(d)), counter-terrorism and rights review (Section 12(e)), treaty studies (Section 12(f)), and promoting research and human rights literacy (Section 12(g), (h)).
2. Bridging International and Municipal Law: Under Section 12(f), the NHRC evaluates conventions such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), ICCPR, ICESCR, CEDAW, and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), and advises Parliament and the Union Executive on bringing municipal laws into conformity with global human rights standards.

2. अंतरराष्ट्रीय व घरेलू कानूनों का समन्वय: धारा 12(f) के तहत एनएचआरसी वैश्विक संधियों (जैसे UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR, UNCRC) का अध्ययन कर भारत सरकार को यह परामर्श देता है कि घरेलू विधियों को अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार मानकों के अनुरूप कैसे सुधारा जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Yes, it is a statutory function under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 12(f) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, studying international human rights treaties and conventions is an explicit statutory function of the National Human Rights Commission. The Commission is legally mandated to evaluate international legal instruments and make constructive recommendations to the government for their effective domestic implementation and compliance.

question_hindi: किसी जिले में बड़े सांप्रदायिक दंगे भड़कने के पश्चात, एक नागरिक समाज संगठन पुलिस की निष्क्रियता और कथित मिलीभगत के संबंध में राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) में याचिका दायर करता है। आयोग स्वतः संज्ञान (suo motu) लेते हुए मौके पर तथ्यात्मक जांच दल भेजने का निर्णय लेता है। आयोग का कौन-सा विशिष्ट प्रभाग (Division) इस प्रकार की जमीनी और तथ्यात्मक जांच संचालित करता है?

question_english: Following a major communal riot in a district, a civil society organization petitions the NHRC regarding alleged state and police inaction. The NHRC takes suo motu cognizance and resolves to dispatch an on-ground investigative fact-finding team. Which specialized division within the NHRC conducts such independent, factual investigations?
options_english: The Law Division, which handles judicial registries and statutory compliance
The Policy Research, Projects and Legal Review Division
The Investigation Division, headed by a senior police officer of the rank of Director General of Police (DGP)
The Human Rights Training, Media and Information Dissemination Division
explanation_english:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has an autonomous, in-house Investigation Division headed by a senior police officer not below the rank of Director General of Police (DGP), assisted by a Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Senior Superintendents of Police (SSPs), and Superintendents of Police (SPs).
Key Legal and Structural Aspects:
1. Section 14 Powers: Under Section 14 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Commission is authorized to utilize the services of any officer or investigation agency of the Central or State Government for inquiries.
2. Role of the Investigation Division: To maintain impartiality when local police forces are accused of bias, complicity, encounter killings, or inaction, the NHRC deploys its own Investigation Division to conduct spot investigations, examine victims, record statements, and gather independent forensic and documentary evidence.
3. Contrast with Other Divisions:
   - Law Division: Headed by a Registrar (Law), handles complaint intake, legal scrutiny, and bench listings.
   - Policy Research Division: Coordinates thematic research, human rights indicators, and treaty compliance.
   - Training Division: Focuses on sensitization programs for civil servants and police personnel.
explanation_hindi:
राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) के पास मानवाधिकार उल्लंघनों की स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष तथ्यात्मक जांच के लिए एक स्वायत्त 'अन्वेषण प्रभाग' (Investigation Division) होता है, जिसका प्रमुख पुलिस महानिदेशक (DGP) रैंक का एक वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधिकारी होता है।
प्रमुख कानूनी एवं संगठनात्मक बिंदु:
1. धारा 14 की शक्तियां: मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 14 के अनुसार, आयोग किसी भी जांच के प्रयोजन हेतु केंद्र अथवा राज्य सरकार के किसी अधिकारी या जांच एजेंसी की सेवाएं ले सकता है।
2. अन्वेषण प्रभाग का कार्य: जब स्थानीय पुलिस पर ही पक्षपात, हिरासत में प्रताड़ना, फर्जी मुठभेड़ या सांप्रदायिक दंगों में निष्क्रियता के आरोप हों, तब एनएचआरसी अपने स्वतंत्र अन्वेषण प्रभाग को मौके पर भेजता है। यह दल गवाहों के बयान दर्ज करता है, साक्ष्य जुटाता है और सीधे आयोग को गोपनीय व निष्पक्ष रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करता है।
3. अन्य प्रभागों से अंतर:
   - विधि प्रभाग: शिकायतों का पंजीकरण, संवीक्षा और न्यायिक फाइलों की प्रस्तुति करता है।
   - नीति अनुसंधान प्रभाग: कानूनों की समीक्षा, मानवाधिकार नीतियों और संधियों पर शोध करता है।
   - प्रशिक्षण प्रभाग: सिविल सेवकों और सुरक्षा बलों के मानवाधिकार संवेदीकरण का कार्य करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The Investigation Division, headed by a Director General of Police

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The National Human Rights Commission operates an autonomous Investigation Division to conduct independent factual inquiries into serious human rights violations. Headed by a senior police officer holding the rank of Director General of Police, this specialized division deploys investigative teams to gather evidence, interview witnesses, and submit detailed factual reports directly to the Commission.
